text:
Sylvia: heads up — Atlas-13B int8 onboarding hit a weird regression on the codegen suite after bucketization changes. failure rate jumped ~12% vs fp16 baseline. Can we triage priority and gating steps? :thinking_face:

Omar: ugh, saw that in nightly dashboards. looks like the prefix cache + bucket split produces diff tokenization length distribution for code tasks. short loops fail more often. :eyes:

Chandra: can you paste the failing examples? quick glance tells me some are prompt-formatting edge cases (missing trailing newline).

Sylvia: pasted sample below (from eval run id 2026-04-12-13):
```
Input: "def fib(n):\n    # compute fib"
Prompt: "Complete the function implementation"
Expected: code with base cases
Model output: truncated loop, missing return on edge case
```

Matt: quantify — is it only codegen or also summarization/test generation?

Sylvia: mostly codegen and unit-test style synth. embedding-based rerank still fine.

Liam: my hunch: quantized linear attention kernel in int8 path underflows on short sequences after bucket remap. we should run the micro-bench with seq_len 8/16/32 and compare logits.

Omar: agree. Suggested immediate action items (short checklist):
- run micro logits compare (seq 8/16/32) against fp16 on same seed
- re-run int8 with old bucketization to isolate change
- collect top-20 diffs and inspect tokens/positions
- add failing prompts to regression set and block release if >10% regression on codenet

Chandra: I'll own the first two. starting runs now. tagging @eval-bot to kick a diff job.

eval-bot: queued job eval-diff-2065432100-run1 (compare logits int8 vs fp16 for atlas-13b). ETA ~45m.

Matt: if it's a kernel numerical issue, we might patch quant scaling or fallback to per-layer fp16 for critical matmuls. but that impacts perf — need cost delta estimate.

Sylvia: for prioritization — product asked if this should be P0 (customer-impacting) or P1. Current recommendation: P1 unless we see regressions on production prompts or Canary traffic.

Liam: quick script to run micro-check:
```
python3 tests/micro_compare.py --model atlas-13b --modes int8 fp16 --seq-lens 8 16 32 --seed 42 --out /tmp/diffs.json
```

Omar: also capture KV cache snapshots and token alignments. add `--dump-cache` flag.

Chandra: ran old-bucket vs new-bucket test. preliminary results: new-bucket int8 vs fp16 shows 11.8% top-1 token mismatch at seq_len 8, old-bucket int8 vs fp16 is 2.1%. Uploading logs to /mnt/runs/2065432100/.

Sylvia: that's a smoking gun — bucket change + int8 interaction. Next steps: revert bucket change on int8 path as a temporary mitigation and add regression test in CI. Can we do a canary revert and measure perf impact?

Omar: I can roll canary revert on staging for dedicated infra. Will monitor latency and cost. If perf drop <4% and reduces reg back to <3% we can lock it behind a flag.

Matt: engineering-side mitigation list for the ticket:
- revert bucket remap for int8 runtime (canary)
- add targeted regression prompts to triage-suite
- investigate quant scaling per-head for short sequences
- long-term: make bucketization quant-aware in compilation phase

Sylvia: thanks. I'll open a formal PRD-lite in the intake tracker with priority P1, link to logs, and assign owners. Can we sync briefly at 16:30 PT?

Liam: 16:30 PT works for me. Omar/Chandra/Matt?

Omar: yes, adding calendar invite.

Chandra: on it. uploading diffs now. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: eval-diff-2065432100-run1 complete — summary: seq8 mismatch 11.8%, seq16 mismatch 6.3%, seq32 mismatch 1.2%. artifacts at s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/2065432100/diffs.json

Sylvia: perfect — will include those numbers in the PRD. tagging stakeholders in the doc. closing this thread for async follow-ups, please update the intake ticket with any new findings. :white_check_mark:
